name: Richard Teets Jr
forbes_bio: Richard Teets is a cofounder of Steel Dynamics, one of the largest steel producers and metals recyclers in the United States.
He cofounded the Fort Wayne, Indiana-based company in 1993 and helped take it public on the Nasdaq in 1996.
He retired as the company's executive vice president for steelmaking and president and chief operating officer of steel operations in 2016.
He owns 3% of the company.

name: Hongbin Sun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2019-2025); Forbes annual (2013-2022); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2003-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Sun Hongbin is the founder and chairman of Sunac China Holdings, one of China's largest real estate developers.
Sunac is headquartered in Tianjin, and its shares trade on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Sunac has expanded into the entertainment and hotel business in the past two years by acquiring assets from China's Wanda Group.
Sun, a U.S. citizen, received his master's degree from Tsinghua University and completed an advanced management program at Harvard Business School.

name: Edgar Sia II
forbes_bio: Edgar Sia II is the chairman of DoubleDragon Properties, the real estate developer he and his partner Tony Tan Caktiong took public in 2014.
The company has been developing commercial and residential properties and reportedly plans to build 100 malls by 2020.
Sia took his grocery chain MerryMart public in June 2020.
An aspiring architect, Sia dropped out of college to start Filipino fast-food label Mang Inasal.
Sia sold a stake in Mang Inasal to Tan Caktiong in 2012.
forbes_facts: His father is part Chinese and his mother is part Japanese.

name: Zhao Dongping
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021); Hurun Global (2021); Hurun China (2020-2021)
forbes_bio: Zhao Dongping is general manager of Anker Innovations Technology, a China supplier of power charging products.
Half of Anker's revenue comes from the U.S. market.
Zhao worked for Dell China's and Google China's sales departments before joining Anker.
Anker is headquartered in Shenzhen, one of China's main electronics industry hubs.

name: Albert Yeung
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2011-2019); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Albert Yeung branched out from his father's watch shop to found leading Hong Kong retailer Emperor Watch & Jewellery.
Emperor Group includes five listed Hong Kong companies.
The group concedes that its entertainment interests, notably Cantopop and film production, are more about publicity for the brand than for revenue.
Emperor's real estate holdings focus on Hong Kong, Beijing and London.
forbes_facts: Yeung holds no corporate office in Emperor Group companies but is the controlling shareholder.
Yeung counts actor Jackie Chan as a friend and investor.
Emperor Hotel in Macau features red-coated faux Coldstream Guards outside and, inside, real gold bars embedded in the lobby floor.

name: Don Ahern
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Don Ahern, a construction equipment tycoon, made his fortune helping build skyscrapers in Las Vegas and other U.S. cities.
In 1978, after graduating high school, he launched Los Arcos Equipment, which began with a fleet of eight scissor lifts.
He purchased his dad's company, Ahern's Trailer and Equipment Rental, in 1990, and later merged Los Arcos into the family firm.
He sold the business in 2022 to United Rentals for $2 billion, pocketing an estimated $600 million after taxes and paying off debts.
Ahern still owns construction equipment maker Xtreme Manufacturing and a 51% stake in Snorkel, which manufactures aerial work platforms and lifts.
forbes_facts: A diehard Republican, Ahern briefly served as finance chair for the Nevada State Republican party.
His Ahern Luxury Boutique Hotel in Las Vegas has become a go-to venue for state and national conservatives to hold events.

name: Analjit Singh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2022); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Analjit Singh is the youngest son of Bhai Mohan Singh, founder of pharma firm Ranbaxy Laboratories.
Today he controls the $4.5 billion (revenue) Max Group, with interests in healthcare, insurance and specialty packaging film.
In recent years, Singh has invested in South Africa where he owns a vineyard and two boutique resorts.
His son, Veer, runs Vana, a private wellness retreat in the northern Indian city of Dehradun.
In February 2025 he settled a three-year-long dispute with estranged wife Neelu Singh, by buying out her 24.15% stake in family holding company Max Ventures.
forbes_facts: The Boston University grad made an early investment in India's telecom sector and made a pile when he sold his stake in that business to Li Ka-shing.
His daughter founded Antara, a senior living community in North India.
In March 2022, his wife Neelu filed a lawsuit alleging mismanagement by her husband. Singh has refuted her allegations.

name: David Katzman
forbes_bio: David Katzman is the CEO of SmileDirectClub, which sells custom teeth aligners.
Katzman's son and his son's friend started the company in 2014.
His investment firm, Camelot Venture Group, provided initial funding for SmileDirectClub.
Katzman had previously invested in direct-to-consumer companies like Quicken Loans and 1-800-Contacts.
SmileDirectClub went public in September 2019; Katzman remains the largest shareholder.

name: Fu Meicheng
appears_on: Forbes annual (2014-2018); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)

name: Fu Gang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2022); Hurun China (2021)
forbes_bio: Fu Gang chairs Qingdao Baheal Medical, a pharmaceuticals supplier headquartered in western China.
Qingdao Baheal Medical went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2021.

name: Mou Jinxiang
forbes_bio: Mou Jinxiang is the ex-chair of Lianhe Chemical Technology, a contract manufacturer of pharmaceuticals and chemicals.
Mou co-founded Lianhe with husband Wang Zhihua, who died in the 1990s.
Daughter Wang Ping is Lianhe's chairman and general manager.
